newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan's annual vehicle output seen rising.
newsitem.headline: Japan's annual vehicle output seen rising.

text.p: Japan's domestic vehicle production is expected to show its first rise in six years this fiscal year, driven by the weaker yen and a host of new models, analysts and industry sources said on Thursday.
Seiji Sugiura, an analyst at Nomura Research, forecast domestic vehicle production for the year to next March at about 10.30 million units, an increase of just over two percent.
Output last year fell five percent.
Sugiura said production at Japan's largest maker Toyota Motor was on target, and that Honda Motor had been producing more vehicles than planned.
"Exports are recovering. Inventories at Toyota and Honda in the United States are declining, so they are expected to increase exports," Sugiura said.
The Japan Automobile Manufacturers Association (JAMA) said on Thursday that domestic production rose 7.3 percent in September from a year earlier to 923,320 vehicles.
"September's gain resulted from good domestic demand for new models. Domestic sales gained in September and exports are rising due to the weaker yen," a JAMA official said.

Production in the first six months to September totalled 4.95 million units, up 0.3 percent from the same period last year. It was the first gain in six years and was due mainly to higher output by Toyota and Honda.

Toyota's first-half domestic production rose 6.2 percent from a year earlier to 1.62 million units, and Honda's rose 11.2 percent to 526,764. Other big makers posted declines, mainly due to delays in the introduction of recreational vehicles.
Japanese carmakers have launched more than 27 new models in the domestic market so far this year and are expected to launch several more by next March, industry sources said.
Overseas sales have also been boosted by a falling yen, which has dropped from a post-war high of 79.75 yen to the dollar in April 1995 to about 112 yen now.

JAMA said domestic vehicle sales rose four percent from a year earlier to 658,427 in September. It said it expects exports in September to have risen about 12 percent from a year earlier. It will announce official figures on October 29.
JAMA said first-half exports were expected to be unchanged from a year earlier. Exports for the same period last year were 1.83 million units, down 15.8 percent.
Automobile industry officials say Japan needs to maintain domestic vehicle production of around 10 million units per year to secure current employment levels.
The automobile-related industry in Japan employs 7.13 million workers, about 10 percent of the total workforce.
